hook: One of the shortest Keter files you will find: a one-line procedure, a two-sentence description, then a table. There is nothing to explain in advance. Read the table slowly, row by row, and let it build.
whyItMatters:
The whole article runs on one strange pair of verbs, going inside and becoming inside, and never explains either. Its tags tie it to the hard-to-destroy reptile and to Dr. Reynders, both of whom appear in the table.

It is a clean example of how far a file can get on pattern and implication alone, with almost no prose.
thingsToNotice:
The rows start small, with a car that already was inside and a run of D-class, then a containment unit where the inside dies. From there the targets escalate: a Finnish city becomes inside while its people going inside turns out to be a working evacuation, and SCP-682 is pointed at again and again until the result is simply Outside.

Then someone turns it on the Foundation itself: the O5s, Punishment, Dr. Reynders, and a hopeful try at Chronology with a 'worth a shot' shrug. The last stretch alternates Transcendence with O5-1, O5-2, O5-3 and O5-4, as if each Overseer is being spent on making it work, and it ends with Transcendence coming back Outside three times in a row. The procedure telling you to keep the thing inside only lands as a joke once you have seen all of this.

related.note: The reptile the table points at again and again.
